_comment: BASELINE FOR tools/supply-chain/audit-actions.sh -- READ docs/adr/ADR-073-supply-chain-pin-actions-and-browsers.md BEFORE EDITING.
WHAT THIS FILE IS. It records every third-party GitHub Action this repository
invokes, the 40-hex commit SHA each one is pinned to, and the release tag that
SHA carried at the moment the pin was last reviewed. audit-actions.sh compares
today's workflow files against these values and fails on any difference.
THIS ONE IS A POLICY, NOT MERELY A TRIPWIRE -- and that makes it the STRONGER
of the three baselines in this directory, which is the opposite of what its
sibling expected-containers.json says about itself. The difference is what the
identifier commits to. A container digest IS its content, so a pin cannot go
bad and that baseline can only tell you a pin changed. An npm version string is
republishable, so expected-plugins.json is a compromise tripwire. A git commit
SHA is content-addressed like a digest AND the thing being pinned is mutable by
default -- `uses: actions/checkout@v4` follows a tag the action's owner can move
onto any commit at will. So this file does something neither sibling can: it
makes the UNPINNED FORM ITSELF a failure. The audit rejects any `uses:`
reference that is not 40 hex characters, whether or not it appears below.
WHY THIS IS NOT PAPERWORK. In March 2025 tj-actions/changed-files had its tags
retargeted onto a commit that dumped CI runner memory -- including secrets --
into the build log, and every workflow in the world pinned to `@v35` executed
it on the next run with no diff to review and no version number changing. A SHA
pin is the documented mitigation. This repository has no secrets today, which
bounds the damage but does not make the pin optional: the `image` job pushes to
GHCR with a token GitHub mints for it, and `perf-trend` is the one job that can
write to the repository.
THE HONEST COST, stated so nobody discovers it as a surprise. A SHA pin freezes
security fixes too. `actions/checkout@v4` would have picked up a patched v4.4.1
on its own; pinned, it will not, and NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY ENFORCES AN
UPGRADE CADENCE -- there is no Dependabot configuration and this audit is
deliberately network-free, so it cannot tell you a newer release exists. That
residual is accepted and recorded in ADR-073; the retiring condition named
there is the adoption of an automated bump, at which point this file becomes
the thing that reviews its pull requests rather than the thing that blocks it.
FIELDS, all mandatory.
sha              -- the 40-hex commit the workflow pins. Lower case.
tag              -- the exact semver release that SHA carried when reviewed,
e.g. v4.4.0. NOT the major alias: `v4` is what we are
moving away from, so recording it here would defeat the
point of having a human-readable record at all.
major            -- the major alias the tag belongs to. Kept separately
because it is what a reader recognises and what the
upstream release notes are indexed by.
reference_count  -- how many `uses:` sites invoke this action. Compared, so
adding a tenth checkout step without updating this file
fails rather than passing silently.
occurrences      -- every tracked file that must carry the reference.
BIDIRECTIONAL: a listed file no longer carrying it fails,
and a workflow file carrying a reference to an action that
is not declared here fails too.
note             -- what the action does here and what moving its pin costs.
HOW TO MOVE A PIN. Resolve the new commit for the tag you intend
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag> --jq .object.sha
read the release notes for what changed, then update the workflow and this file
IN THE SAME REVIEWED COMMIT. Never update this file to silence a red build: a
SHA you did not deliberately choose is exactly the tj-actions failure mode with
one extra step.

actions/checkout.note: Checks the repository out in every job that reads a tracked file. The most-invoked action here and the one the tj-actions incident maps onto most directly, because it runs first and therefore runs before any step that could observe it misbehaving.

actions/setup-java.note: Provisions the JDK for the `build` job and for the Sonar scan. Moving this pin does not change the JDK -- the version is chosen by the `with:` block, not by the action -- so a bump here is a bump of the provisioning code only.

actions/cache.note: Caches the Maven repository and the SonarQube scanner download. A cache action is a higher-value target than its mundane name suggests: it both reads and writes a store that later steps trust, so a compromised build of it could poison a dependency tree that no lockfile check would notice.

actions/upload-artifact.note: Publishes build reports, the k6 results, the two CI images the `e2e` job consumes, and the three end-to-end artifacts. Paired with actions/download-artifact below -- the two must be kept on compatible majors, because v4 artifacts are not readable by a v3 download and the failure is a confusing 404 rather than a version error.

actions/setup-node.note: Provisions Node 22 for the `ui` job, the `supply-chain` job and the `e2e` job. The `e2e` site is the one that matters for ADR-073: it still installs Node on the runner because the Playwright suite's own npm tree is installed there, while the browsers now come from a digest-pinned container instead of a CDN download.

actions/download-artifact.note: Retrieves the k6 summary for the `perf-trend` job, the `ci-images` archive for the `e2e` job, and the `e2e-results` archive for the `e2e-report` job. Must stay on a major compatible with actions/upload-artifact above.

docker/setup-buildx-action.note: Configures the buildx builder the `image` job builds both production images with. Note this is the same tool the container baseline's verification instructions tell you to run by hand (`docker buildx imagetools inspect`), so a change here changes how digests are resolved as well as how images are built.

docker/build-push-action.note: Builds the API image from `Dockerfile` and the front-end image from `ui/Dockerfile`. The highest-consequence action in the workflow, because its output is the artifact that ships -- a compromised build of it could alter an image that every later job, including `e2e`, would then test and pass.

docker/login-action.note: Authenticates to GHCR before the push, on `github.event_name == 'push'` only. This is the single site in the workflow that handles a credential of any kind -- the token GitHub mints for the job -- which is precisely the class of step the tj-actions payload existed to harvest.
